A0019.title: Identity Security Audit
A0019.definition: Conducting continuous security audits of user accounts to detect account risks in a timely manner.
A0019.description: Similar to the risk monitoring mechanism of risk control strategies (A0015), identity behavior monitoring and risk assessment is also an audit-based protective measure. However, the two differ in their protection subjects and objects: risk control protects the business from users, while identity behavior auditing protects users from attackers. Identity security auditing is a commonly used means of assessing identity security. After an anomaly is detected, it needs to be combined with other identity measures such as re-authentication (A0018), multi-factor authentication (A0007), and forced password reset (A0012).
A0019.limitation: Generally, identity security auditing relies on detecting abnormal account behavior, which requires a certain amount of time and data as a reference baseline. Additionally, in some cases, identity security auditing has a certain degree of latency — subsequent handling or loss mitigation is required after a risk is identified.

A0019-002.title: Invitation Code Mechanism
A0019-002.definition: Requiring users to present a limited-distribution invitation code at registration as an entry credential, thereby restricting the registration gateway to invited users.
A0019-002.description:
The invitation code mechanism binds registration permission to one-time or quantity-limited codes, turning open registration into an invite-only flow and raising the cost of bulk registration at the source. Codes can be centrally generated and targeted by administrators, or issued by existing users within quotas; it is common in beta products, communities, and products under strict risk control.

It can be combined with code-to-inviter binding, device fingerprinting (A0021), and human verification (A0001): each code is limited to a single device and account, the inviter bears joint liability for the invitee's behavior, compressing the room for illicit actors to spin up accounts at scale with farming tools. When codes show anomalous consumption (multiple IPs activating in a short window, device clustering), the related codes and accounts can be frozen immediately.
A0019-002.limitation: The invitation code mechanism is unsuitable for mass-market open-registration products, as it notably raises acquisition cost and lowers conversion; illicit actors can bypass it by purchasing invite quotas from registered accounts, collecting codes publicly on social platforms, or routing bulk activations through SMS-receiving platforms. Once codes leak at scale the gating effect is lost, so it must be paired with device fingerprinting and behavior auditing (A0019) for ongoing verification.

A0019-003.title: Friend-Assisted Authentication
A0019-003.definition: A mechanism that uses the user's friends to assist in authenticating the user's identity.
A0019-003.description: During user registration or verification, the user must select their friends. The system sends verification messages to these friends, and the user can only complete registration after passing verification through these friends.
A0019-003.limitation: If the user has no friends or the friends are unwilling to assist with verification, the user cannot complete registration, causing significant collateral damage to new users and those with weak social connections. Additionally, illicit actors can accumulate auxiliary accounts through account farming or mutual friend-adding, fabricating social relationships to bypass friend-assisted verification, rendering this mechanism ineffective.
